neighbours.label: An adjective or possessive naming a learned profession or discipline used as a modifier of a role, body or title (scientific adviser, medical officer, Teachers' Union, the Artists' Guild, Scientific Committee)
fire: In 1951 she became scientific adviser to the Ministry of Supply.
The town's chief medical officer ordered the wells to be sealed.
The Teachers' Union called a strike over class sizes.
He read a paper to the Royal Medical and Surgical Society.
The Artists' Guild rented a hall for its annual show.
She joined the scientific staff of the observatory in 1924.
The journal's medical editor rejected the paper twice.
He was elected to the Scientific Committee of the Antarctic expedition.
quiet: In 1951 she became a trusted adviser to the Ministry of Supply.
The town's chief officer ordered the wells to be sealed.
The drivers' union called a strike over long shifts.
He read a paper to the local history society.
The Rotary Club rented a hall for its annual show.
She joined the catering staff of the observatory in 1924.
The journal's senior editor rejected the paper twice.
He was elected to the steering committee of the Antarctic expedition.

predictions: Role and body names modified by scientific/medical/Teachers'/Artists' reach 0.3-0.9 on the modifier, strongest for 'scientific adviser'. The same roles and bodies with non-discipline modifiers (trusted adviser, drivers' union, Rotary Club, steering committee, catering staff) stay under 0.15.
short: discipline modifier of a role or body
notes: Probe: 'appointed scientific adviser' 0.899, "The Artist's Way" 0.395 ("'s"), 'Scientific American' 0.394, 'Teachers College' 0.361, 'British Medical Journal' 0.122 only; 'the scientific method' 0.335 (the common adjective also fires), 'medical team' 0.230, "artist's studio" 0.153, floor 0.068. Card: ' scientific' x4, ' Scientific' x4, ' Medical' x3, '’s' x3 before advisor/Act/Journal/Voice/College/Outlook (max 61, layer 26); the - pole suppresses ' physicists', ' economists', ' scientists', so this pole promotes profession nouns. The risk is that the plain adjective (scientific method 0.335) fires as much as the role modifier.
